mechanisms.statement: Each problem has a fixed answer distribution under one model, prompt and T 1.0; a plurality vote estimates its mode. Going from 4 to 9 samples converts problems where the right value is the plurality but lost a 4-sample tie or a 2-2 split; problems whose right share sits below a repeated wrong value, or near zero, stay lost. Votes therefore plateau below pass@k, and an even k (12) brings ties back, adding about one problem over 9.

holds_against.why: Wang's majority@8 is 2.5 points over majority@4 (about +12 problems), but that is an expectation with random ties; our 446 already sits above their 4-vote level, so only the room to pass@4 467 is left, giving about +6 at k = 9.
43 % of 4-vote failures with a right sample lose to an agreeing wrong group, which more samples do not fix; the other 57 % are singleton ties that odd k dissolves, the source of the predicted gain.

forecasts.reason: 446 at k=4 plus about 7 tied or 2-2 problems won by plurality at k=9, minus a few lost to repeated wrong values; pass@4 467 is the ceiling.

mechanisms.statement: A sample that runs to the token cap writes no answer and casts no vote. A model whose wrong attempts end unfinished (Think-SFT) gets a vote close to its pass@k; one whose wrong attempts end in a finished guess (RL, the base) loses more to selection. Raising the cap or adding finishing weight turns abstentions into votes; at a low right rate these new votes add right answers but also break single-answer wins, so vote gains trail single-sample gains.

holds_against.why: The base caps often yet its vote is 13 below pass@4 205: its cap hits fall on problems it cannot solve while its finished answers are wrong 36 % of the time, so abstention removes few wrong votes.

The base's fresh2026 vote gains 8.5 over its single with 40 % cap hits, close to RL's +6.5 at 15 %: with finished precision of 36 % abstention cannot help; the mechanism needs high finished precision, as Think-SFT's 80 %.

forecasts.reason: At 16k 29 % of samples abstain and the vote 241 is near pass@4 244; at 32k 91 of 93 cut answers finish, 25 % right: about +10 new problems won, about -5 single-answer wins broken.

A cell posted because it was best of several tried overstates its mean and new samples fall back by about one sd; pre-registered cells do not.

mechanisms.statement: Ending is a sampled event: wherever the model could wrap up, it emits a stop or answer token with some probability h, so a long attempt survives to the cap with probability about (1-h)^n. A cap hit is a lost race. Scaling the wrap-up probability by a factor raises each problem's cap probability to a power; a larger cap gives the race more draws but adds right answers only where the reasoning was still on track.

holds_against.why: Forced commits on the 77 cap-hit answers are right on at most 2: ending a lost race does not make its reasoning right; the mechanism claims only that ending is stochastic, which the restart gain (161 to 172 on the 328) supports.

RL fixes the base's cap-hit problems at the rate of equally hard finished-wrong ones: the number of wrap-up chances needed grows with problem length, so cap hits track difficulty, as the race predicts.

mechanisms.statement: A fine-tuned model sampled at T 1.0 in a context unlike its training format (raw template plus the base's cue) has flatter next-token distributions. The extra entropy shows late in long traces as drift: script switches into Chinese, restarts, longer answers and more cap hits. In its own chat template the distribution is sharper, so traces are shorter and fewer are cut at 16,384; at a 32,768 cap the formats nearly converge because most cut traces finish anyway.

mechanisms.statement: A weight edit adds a roughly fixed logit offset toward finishing and hold-on tokens. At T 1.0 sampling degrades into word strings only where that offset exceeds the host's margin between its top token and the rest. The base has flat, high-entropy distributions and breaks near 3x the top-8 directions; Think-SFT, trained on traces, has sharp distributions and tolerates large offsets. Edits that write the same tokens add their offsets, so stacking them acts as a larger dose.

holds_against.why: Think-SFT does lose points at 4x the full RL delta (227 to 213), but stays coherent with 33 cap hits, while the base collapses to 117 at only 3x the top-8 part.

The base with 1.5x the full delta still scores 453 although 34 answers end in word salad: its top-8 component there is only 1.5x, below the base's breaking point near 3x, and the salad tails are the first sign of it.
